To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nosocomial infections are a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and cost in the USA, that there is an increasing awareness that nosocomial infection control is an essential part of the total quality of health care, and that the CDC guidelines for prevention and control of nosocomial infection are the primary means of disseminating information on effective prevention and control strategies.

the incidence of nosocomial infection is high, that nosocomial infections cause significant morbidity and mortality, that nosocomials infections prolong hospital stays, and that the cost of nosocomial treatment is substantial.

the development and evaluation of methods for the prevention of nosocomials infections.
the development, implementation, and evaluation of infection prevention and control strategies in acute care hospitals in the USA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most important priority for nosocomial prevention and control is the prevention of infections at the four most important sites: the bloodstream, surgical wounds, the urinary tract, and the respiratory tract.

the national priority for nosocomial infections is the development of a system for surveillance, analysis and reporting of nosocomial infection data that will allow for timely and effective interventions.

the national priorities for noscomial infection prevention and surveillance are: (1) to reduce the incidence of infections caused by emerging nosocomial pathogens and (2) to reduce the morbidity and mortality from nosocomial infection by preventing or reducing infections in selected high risk patients and by reducing the incidence of nosocomial infection caused by selected pathogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not doing enough in terms of prevention and control of infections.
we have a lot to do, and we need to do it better.
there is an urgent need for more research in nosocomial infection control and prevention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDC is a leader in setting national priorities and disseminating information about prevention of infections in healthcare facilities.
the CDC is committed to the prevention and control of nosocomial infection and is actively involved in this endeavor.
there is a need for a national nosocomial infection control program in the USA.
